memory_candidates.content: The multi-subagent continuation loop pattern enables automatic context exhaustion recovery: (1) agent writes handoff + progress file before returning partial, (2) skill detects handoff_path in metadata, (3) skill spawns successor with continuation_context injected into delegation context, (4) loop continues up to max 3 times tracked via .continuation-loop-guard file. Per-subagent git commits (Stage 6b) ensure progress is checkpointed. This pattern generalizes to any skill delegating to long-running subagents.

Use a .loop-guard file in the task directory to track iteration counts across potential skill interruptions. The file stores session_id, continuation_count, max_continuations, and timestamps. On loop entry, read the guard; on each iteration, update it; on final cleanup, remove it. This provides resilience against SubagentStop hooks or unexpected terminations mid-loop.

Per-subagent git commits inside a continuation loop provide better recoverability than a single final commit. After each subagent returns (implemented, partial, or failed), commit with a phase-specific message before deciding whether to spawn a successor. This ensures earlier progress is preserved if a later continuation fails or the loop is interrupted.
